## New

- **Esc stops a reply, after asking.** `Esc` in an empty chat input while a reply streams asks "Stop the response?": `Enter` stops, `Esc` keeps going. What the reply wrote and your unsent text are kept, and the stopped turn is saved for Resume. The Stop button declares the key with `aria-keyshortcuts`. See "Stop, Resume and recovering a turn".
- **Editing an earlier message keeps the replaced turns.** Before the edit runs, the conversation is saved as "<title> (before edit)" in History, and a line above the input offers Undo (the conversation comes back; the edited version is kept in the copy instead) and View. The terminal agent saves the same copy before it rewinds for an edit; `/resume` opens it.

## Behaviour changes

- **No single key stops running work.** `Ctrl+L`, New Session, opening a chat from History and switching, closing or archiving a session tab now ask "Stop the agent and start a new chat?" (or open, or switch) while a reply streams, a tool call waits for approval, a tool runs or a loop runs. `Enter` stops the work the way Stop does and switches, saving the chat with its reply marked stopped; `Esc` keeps working. Pressing the key again or holding it never answers. With nothing running nothing is asked, so there is no "don't ask again". The Command Palette's **Stop Response**, and the Stop button reached with `Enter` or `Space`, ask the same way; a click on Stop still stops at once.
- **Terminal agent: `Esc`, `Ctrl+C` and `Ctrl+D` ask first.** `Esc` while the agent works, and `Ctrl+C` on an empty prompt while it works, ask "Stop the response? enter to stop · esc to keep going". `Ctrl+C` with text typed no longer clears it at once: it asks "Clear the input?", and `Up` brings cleared text back. Two `Ctrl+C` presses within a second exit at once only while idle; while a turn, a tool call or a loop runs they ask "Exit and stop the agent?", and a held key's auto-repeat never counts as the second press. `Ctrl+D` asks the same while work runs or text is typed.
- **Terminal agent: a stopped reply is kept.** What the model wrote before Stop stays in the conversation and is saved with the session, marked as stopped; `Enter` on the empty prompt resumes from it instead of asking again from scratch.
- **Terminal agent: `Esc` on a permission prompt skips that call.** `Esc` (or `Ctrl+C`) is now "No, skip this call": the model gets the denied result and the turn goes on. "No, and tell Continue what to do differently" (`n`) still ends the turn, after asking "Stop the response?".
